title: Define skillification as a general practice
description: Forward anchor: /design/skillify/README.md. Define skillification for a general audience as transforming knowledge and recurring practice into activatable, testable capability. Cover activation boundaries, capability scope, process/reference forms, completion, evidence, progressive disclosure, host profiles, GLOBAL-to-parent AGENTS assembly, evaluation, lifecycle, and failure modes. Rekon AGENTS modularization is one application, not the definition.
acceptance_criteria: Independent model-suffixed designs are compared and synthesized; an accepted canonical README defines general vocabulary, candidate criteria, method, capability contract, Markdown README/SKILL/GLOBAL host profile, parent-scoped AGENTS assembly, routing/process/context evaluations, lifecycle, and anti-patterns without depending on rekon migration details.

title: Assemble AGENTS.md from GLOBAL.md fragments
description: Build deterministic tooling that discovers declared GLOBAL.md fragments from knowledge modules and assembles the global AGENTS.md. This improves data locality and per-topic history: contributors edit their local GLOBAL.md, not a monolith. Define ordering, identity, duplicate detection, generated-file markers, and verification without automatic pruning of undeclared artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: A documented deterministic command assembles AGENTS.md from declared GLOBAL.md inputs; duplicate identities and unstable ordering fail clearly; generated output is reproducible; source fragments remain canonical; tests cover ordering and failure behavior.
notes:
2026-09-02: delegated from session ses_fa19cd46bffeBW6dPrBzttf4Gv using marked, gray-matter, and existing gunshi integration. Fragment-local metadata owns identity/order; an explicit manifest declares inputs; production AGENTS.md remains untouched.

2026-09-02: implemented the gunshi agents command with deterministic assembly, provenance, duplicate/path/Markdown validation, atomic writes, UTF-8 per-fragment and total context cost, and non-writing check mode. Independent standards/spec review found 9 standards concerns and 6 spec concerns; fixes applied. Coordinator additionally rejected absolute output declarations and outputs that collide with manifests or source fragments, and replaced the misleading string-bytes API. Verified 78 tests, tsgo, oxlint, tsdown, targeted oxfmt, Pandoc, and whitespace checks. Production manifest remains deliberately deferred until every monolith section has a GLOBAL source.
close_reason: Implemented and documented deterministic AGENTS.md assembly from explicit GLOBAL.md manifests using marked, gray-matter, and gunshi. The command rejects identity/order/path/Markdown conflicts, prevents source/config overwrite, records provenance and UTF-8 context cost, writes atomically, and verifies stale output without writing. Independent standards/spec review and coordinator hardening complete; 78 tests and all targeted gates pass. Production manifest remains intentionally deferred until all monolith sections have fragment sources.

title: rekon ln: CLI utility to apply lowercase symlinks
description:
A standalone CLI utility (gunshi-based) that scans directories and applies the lowercase symlink strategy from [deleted:rekon-symlink-strategies].

Usage: `rekon ln [path...]` (defaults to cwd)
- `-R` / `--no-recursive` to make it non-recursive (default is recursive)
- Scans path components and creates lowercase symlinks for mixed-case directories
- Should use existing symlink libraries from the project
- Idempotent: skips if lowercase path already exists
acceptance_criteria:
- gunshi-based CLI command under rekon
- Defaults to scanning cwd, accepts path arguments
- -R flag makes it non-recursive (recursive by default)
- Creates lowercase symlinks for mixed-case path components
- Idempotent
- Uses existing symlink utilities from the project
close_reason: Superseded by rekon resimplify command and simplify dl step

title: Add symlink transforms for alternate case/punctuation
description:
Add capability to create symlinks with alternate transformations of project names.

Example use cases:
- Lowercase: `rektide/MyProject` → symlink `rektide/myproject`
- Remove punctuation: `rektide/my-project` → symlink `rektide/myproject`
- Combined: `rektide/My-Project` → symlink `rektide/myproject`

This helps with discoverability when project names have different casing or punctuation in different contexts (e.g., GitHub uses lowercase in URLs but repos may have mixed case).

title: Add interpolation-execution mode to interpolate command
description:
After the interpolate command has been created, add an execution mode that can run the interpolated result as a shell command. This would allow users to interpolate variables into command templates and then execute them, similar to how opencode handles commands with interpolated arguments.

Example usage:
```bash
rekon interpolate -t 'echo "Hello $1"' world --execute
# Would output: Hello world

rekon interpolate -t 'ls -la $1' /tmp --execute
# Would run: ls -la /tmp
```

This would be useful for:
- Testing command templates with variable arguments
- Executing commands with variable substitutions without full opencode
- Creating reusable command templates with positional parameters
- Testing prompt/ file templates before using them with opencode

title: Create install-commands subcommand
description:
Implement `install-commands` gunshi subcommand that:
- Scans all markdown/mdx files in prompt/ recursively
- Creates symlinks in ~/.config/opencode/command/
- Checks symlink status with readlink before creating
- Reports per-file status: "already-done", "done", "error-existing-file"
- Supports -f flag to force overwrite existing files
- Creates directory if needed
- Uses async/promises (node:fs/promises) not sync operations
acceptance_criteria:
- install-commands subcommand exists in command/
- Finds all .md and .mdx files in prompt/ recursively
- Creates symlinks to ~/.config/opencode/command/
- Reports status per file: "already-done", "done", "error-existing-file"
- -f flag forces overwrite of existing files
- Uses async/promises from node:fs/promises
- Passes typecheck and lint
- Files are executable with shebang
